title: Denominator from a linear recurrence
statement:
Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C(T)=\sum_{n\geq0}c_nT^n\in K[[T]]$ a formal power series [def-weil-formal-power-series]. Let $m\geq0$, $d\geq1$ be integers and $a_0,\ldots,a_{d-1}\in K$ such that $(c_n)$ satisfies the linear recurrence of order $d$ with coefficients $a_0,\ldots,a_{d-1}$ from the index $m$ on [def-weil-eventual-linear-recurrence]: $c_{n+d}+a_{d-1}c_{n+d-1}+\cdots+a_0c_n=0$ for $n\geq m$. Put
$$
Q(T)=1+a_{d-1}T+a_{d-2}T^2+\cdots+a_0T^d\in K[T]
$$
[def-weil-polynomial-ring], so $[T^0]Q=1$ and $[T^j]Q=a_{d-j}$ for $1\leq j\leq d$ [def-weil-polynomial-coefficient]. Then $Q(0)=1$, and the product $QC\in K[[T]]$ (with $Q$ regarded as a power series [def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series]) is a polynomial $P\in K[T]$ with $[T^N]P=0$ for every $N\geq m+d$; explicitly $[T^N]P=c_N+\sum_{j=1}^{\min(N,d)}a_{d-j}c_{N-j}$ for $0\leq N<m+d$.

source.place: Ch. II, §27, proof of Lemma 27.9, p. 157 (quoting Bourbaki, Algèbre, IV.5, Exercise 3(a): f lies in k(t) iff its coefficients satisfy a linear relation λ_1a_n+…+λ_ra_{n+r-1}=0 for all n≥d; stated, not proved); the direction 'recurrence implies rational'

proof.text: By the definition of the displayed polynomial Q, its coefficient at degree 0 is 1 and its coefficient at degree j is a_{d-j} for 1 <= j <= d; all coefficients at degrees j>d are zero. The coefficient-preserving polynomial-to-power-series map therefore gives Q(0)=1.

source.place: ## Proof, the denominator construction in the (3) implies (1) paragraph

proof.text: For every N>=0, the coefficient of T^N in QC is the finite convolution of the coefficients of Q and C. Since Q has coefficients q_0=1, q_j=a_{d-j} for 1<=j<=d, and q_j=0 for j>d, this coefficient is c_N + sum_{j=1}^{min(N,d)} a_{d-j} c_{N-j}. In particular this is the displayed formula for every N<m+d.

source.place: ## Proof, the coefficient comparison in the (3) implies (1) paragraph

proof.text: If N>=m+d, put n=N-d. Then n>=m and N>=d. Reindexing the given recurrence at n gives c_N + sum_{j=1}^d a_{d-j}c_{N-j}=0. The coefficient formula from the convolution therefore shows that [T^N](QC)=0 for every N>=m+d.

source.place: ## Proof, the recurrence implies the coefficients of QC vanish beyond m+d

proof.text: The coefficient sequence of QC is zero from index m+d onward by the preceding calculation, so it is finitely supported. By the definition of the polynomial ring there is a polynomial P in K[T] with exactly these coefficients. The coefficient-preserving injective map from polynomials to power series then identifies QC with P in K[[T]], and the coefficient formula and vanishing assertion above give all stated properties of P.
